newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes ease on nervous wet Brent, heat build.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes ease on nervous wet Brent, heat build.

text.p: U.S. crudes sank Tuesday on losses in the futures market brought on by sentiment low distillate stock levels were being replenished heading into the winter season, traders said.

Market calls for a 1-3 million barrel build in the weekly American Petroleum Institute (API) inventory report were met when distillate levels came in nearly 3.6 million barrels higher in the post-NYMEX report.
Drastic declines in the value of dated Brent failed to put a dent in Louisiana domestic grade values. Wet Brents were sold Tuesday at Dec Brent minus 43 and 38 cents.
December West Texas Intermediate/Cushing ended at $24.10-$24.20, down more than 60 cts from Monday's close.
The spread between Dec/Jan WTI hovered around 40 cts all session, closing into 34-36 cts at times before widening out.
API inventory data showed the year-on-year gap between this week's distillate stocks and same week 1995 a wide 12 million barrels.

Late outright crude values declined on pressure from the heating oil sector. Crude stocks actually experienced a draw, logged down 2.53 million barrels, and gasoline stocks were off 3.83 million barrels.
For the grades, Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James was last sold at a 71 cts premium to the WTI marker, and was quoted between +70-+75 cts for the session.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire firmed slightly to end at 75-80 cts over the WTI/Cushing, with last deals done at a hefty +75 cts.
Midland/WTI remained steady, getting done at 5-6 cts over the WTI, traders said.
Sour crudes remained pressured by the flux of heavy supplies from Canada and the new round of U.S. government Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) sales.
West Texas Sour/Midland was sold at a $1.49 discount to the WTI, while Eugene Island attracted a deal minus $1.07.
December Postings Plus ended steady, talked at $2.13-$2.16.
